title: 24-layer HfO2/SiO2 dual-band stack with narrowed perturbation bounds on inner layers
scientific_hypothesis: Reducing the perturbation radius from ±12 nm to ±8 nm for layers 7-16 will increase sampling density near the current local optimum, allowing the optimizer to resolve gradient structure that was previously masked by excessive exploration volume, and should produce a measurable increase in best_target_score if the current solution is near but not at the local optimum.
design_principle: Recalled thin-film optimization practice suggests that multilayer dielectric stacks have complex thickness-dependent interference patterns where small thickness changes (5-10 nm) can significantly shift spectral features. Quarter-wave stacks centered at different wavelengths require different optical thicknesses, and the dual-band requirement (high reflection at 300-450 nm, high transmission at 1000-1700 nm) creates competing constraints that benefit from fine-grained thickness tuning rather than coarse exploration.
proposed_topology: 24-layer stack: air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | fused silica substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for layers 7-16 (10 inner layers) with perturbation bounds ±8 nm, layers 1-6 and 17-24 fixed at current best candidate values
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
Maintain physical validity (no negative thicknesses, manufacturable layer thicknesses)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 24 (within 30-layer limit)
All thicknesses must remain positive and above approximately 15 nm for reliable deposition
HfO2 and SiO2 are standard e-beam evaporation or sputtering materials
theory_basis: Recalled knowledge: Quarter-wave optical thickness at wavelength λ requires physical thickness d = λ/(4n) where n is refractive index
Recalled knowledge: HfO2 has higher refractive index (~2.0-2.1) than SiO2 (~1.45-1.5) in visible-NIR range, making them suitable high/low index pairs
Recalled knowledge: Dual-band filters often use chirped or aperiodic layer sequences rather than simple periodic stacks to achieve different behavior at different wavelengths
Recalled knowledge: Gradient-based thickness optimization converges faster when initialized near a known good solution with bounded perturbation
Recalled knowledge: 20-30 layer dielectric stacks are common for demanding spectral filtering applications
expected_advantages: Higher sampling density near current optimum should reveal whether further improvement is possible within the local basin
Fixing outer layers reduces optimization dimensionality while allowing inner layers to compensate for spectral mismatches
Deterministic grid walk eliminates randomness that could obscure whether improvements come from strategy or luck
known_risks: Uncertain whether 24 layers is optimal versus 26 or 28 layers within the 30-layer limit - this route does not test layer count
Uncertain about exact refractive index dispersion of HfO2 and SiO2 in the 300-1700 nm range; measured data from material catalog will be used but I do not know the exact values from memory
Uncertain whether the current best candidate (target_score ~0.942) is near global optimum or trapped in local optimum; narrowing perturbation may not escape local basin if one exists
The ±8 nm bound is a design choice based on recalled practice, not validated by literature; may be too restrictive if larger changes are needed
What would settle these: refractive index dispersion curves from material catalog, comparison with routes that vary layer count, comparison with routes using wider perturbation bounds
execution_request_english: Optimize a 24-layer planar dielectric stack on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials: alternating HfO2 and SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers, starting with HfO2 at the air side. Initialize from the current best candidate thickness vector: [22.0, 80.0, 21.0, 106.0, 61.0, 44.0, 31.0, 51.0, 36.0, 59.0, 39.0, 61.0, 40.0, 61.0, 42.0, 64.0, 68.0, 72.0, 47.0, 61.0, 45.0, 76.0, 39.0, 27.0] nm. Apply deterministic grid walk optimization with perturbation bounds of ±8 nm on layers 7-16 (indices 6-15 in zero-based counting, corresponding to thicknesses 31.0, 51.0, 36.0, 59.0, 39.0, 61.0, 40.0, 61.0, 42.0, 64.0 nm in the baseline). Keep layers 1-6 and 17-24 fixed at baseline values. Spectral objectives: maximize transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band, maximize reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Use coherent transfer-matrix method. Wavelength sampling should cover both bands adequately. Polarization: unpolarized or average of TE and TM. Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal) unless otherwise specified in problem. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and final thicknesses_nm array.
revision_reason: Continuation of control route with narrowed perturbation radius (±12 nm to ±8 nm) for active zone layers 7-16, replacing random-search seeding with deterministic grid walk centered on current best candidate thickness vector to increase sampling density near local optimum
